title: The Greek Alphabet
description: Learn the Greek letters and begin recognizing words in their original script.
context: Ancient Greek is written with an alphabet of 24 letters. Before worrying about grammar, the first goal is simply to recognize the letters and read words aloud.

grammar.title: The alphabet
grammar.explanation: Greek has 24 letters. Most have distinct uppercase and lowercase forms.

example.greek: Α α — Β β — Γ γ
example.note: Learn to recognize the shapes before worrying about perfect pronunciation.

grammar.title: Two forms of sigma
grammar.explanation: Sigma is written σ inside a word and ς at the end of a word.

example.note: The first sigma is σ; the final sigma is ς.

grammar.title: Marks above letters
grammar.explanation: Greek texts contain accents and breathing marks. At first, learn to recognize the underlying word without trying to master every mark.

example.note: The marks are part of normal printed Greek, but they should not prevent you from beginning to read.

texts.title: The Greek Alphabet
texts.greek: Α α  Β β  Γ γ  Δ δ  Ε ε  Ζ ζ  Η η  Θ θ  Ι ι  Κ κ  Λ λ  Μ μ  Ν ν  Ξ ξ  Ο ο  Π π  Ρ ρ  Σ σ/ς  Τ τ  Υ υ  Φ φ  Χ χ  Ψ ψ  Ω ω
readingHints: Read slowly from left to right and learn the uppercase and lowercase forms together.
Notice that sigma has two lowercase forms: σ and final ς.
Try recognizing λόγος, θεός, ἄνθρωπος and ἀρχή before moving on.
